studies.label: Main experiment: three tasks crossed with six team/persona conditions
studies.cluster_se_treatment: Triads were randomized (PDF p. 2). Individual performance uses a REML linear mixed model with a group random intercept; primary fixed-effect inference uses CR2 standard errors clustered by group with Satterthwaite degrees of freedom. Discussion quality uses one observation per group and OLS with CR2 inference (PDF pp. 12-13, section 3.11). EMM tables additionally print model-based uncertainty. The covariance estimator for analytical pairwise comparisons is not explicitly identified in Table 30.

studies.country: Individual countries not stated; participants span North America/Central America, South America, Europe, Africa, Asia and Australia (PDF p. 4, Table 1).
studies.task: Participants wrote an AGI-centered movie plot individually before and after a group discussion; separate task cells in the same experiment completed survival-item ranking or an autonomous-vehicle ethical dilemma (PDF pp. 5-7, section 3.2-3.3; PDF p. 28, Appendix A).

estimates.question: after_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Two independent researchers trained in education and psychology, blinded to condition, rated originality, elaboration and coherence on five-point rubrics; ratings were averaged across raters. The composite performance gain is post-task minus baseline and was standardized before analysis. Exact aggregation of the story dimensions and the standardization reference population are not fully specified (PDF pp. 9-11, sections 3.7 and 3.9; PDF pp. 32-33, Appendix C, Table 9).

regression.model: REML linear mixed model: Task * Condition + (1 | group_id); Creative and H3 are the reference cell; no post-treatment covariates; CR2 inference clustered by group.

estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Two independent, blinded researchers trained in education and psychology rated the group chat transcript on idea generation and sharing, collaborative engagement, and progression and synthesis. Each dimension uses a five-point rubric; ratings are averaged across raters and dimensions to give one group score, then standardized for analysis (PDF pp. 9-13, sections 3.7, 3.9 and 3.11; PDF pp. 32-33, Appendix C, Table 8). This is interaction quality during creative ideation, not a final-story creativity score.

open_items: The underlying generative model, provider, version and release year are not stated. Persona prompts alone do not establish a model identifier (PDF pp. 7-8 and 29-31).

Per-arm randomized people counts and per-arm randomized/analyzed group counts are not printed. The entry count is not established as a randomized count. People counts in Table 2 are retained as analyzed counts in the section 3.1 context; no group counts are inferred from people counts (PDF pp. 3-6).

The creative score aggregation and standardization denominator/reference population are not fully specified. Raw arm means and participant-level SDs are absent; printed marginal means and SEs are not descriptive SDs (PDF pp. 9-13; PDF pp. 51-53).
Separate arm effects/statistics for the originality, elaboration, coherence and discussion-rubric components are not printed (PDF p. 11, Table 6; PDF p. 33, Tables 8-9).

The precise survival error-score formula and scorer are unstated; the paper calls the outcome improvement and interprets higher reported gains as better. Table 30 does not explicitly identify whether its pairwise SEs use CR2 or the conventional LMM covariance estimator (PDF pp. 7, 11, 13 and 16-17; PDF pp. 51-53).

No default AI persona is identified, so AI-design arm orientation is a coding convention documented in the analytical records. Printed contrast signs and CI endpoints have been preserved (PDF p. 7, section 3.4; PDF p. 53, Table 30).

BDI is Balanced Detection Index in the methods but is called baseline depression/depressive symptoms in Appendices E/G. These adjusted and moderation analyses are excluded because the operational definition is post-task detection (PDF pp. 5, 10-11, 38 and 56).

The external coded-exemplar dataset and moderation XLSX files are named without an access URL; no separate files were available in the supplied retrieval record. They are not needed for the extracted full-sample contrasts (PDF p. 10, section 3.7; PDF pp. 56-58, Appendix G).

The exploratory discussion-quality contrast entries repeat across task and BDI levels in Table 37; their intended scale requires the named external XLSX. No number from that moderator-conditional table is used as a full-sample effect (PDF p. 57).

Screening omitted survival-ranking outcomes from its creative-output map. This extraction retains the complete printed analytical pairwise comparisons as convergent under the explicit Phase 2 rule; these records have null form_outcome_id and are never pooled.
notes: Extraction date: 2026-10-11. Read the entire supplied markdown in order, including references and all appendices, and checked cited PDF text with PyMuPDF; table recovery was also checked for the main numerical pages. Only the main randomized experiment appears in studies; the independent humanness pilot is listed in not_extracted. The main experiment remains one study across all task domains. The analyzed study count covers all tasks; no creative-task total or pairwise total was calculated. All extracted arm names follow screening. Individual performance-gain records are immediate after_ai; transcript discussion quality is with_ai. The all-human group provides human partners, hence ai_vs_active. For the main Creative contrasts the CR2 columns are used; conventional inference for the identical coefficients is not duplicated as another estimate. Arm marginal means and their model-based SEs are identified explicitly. p_value contains the original unadjusted p-value; source rows preserve the printed Holm-adjusted values as well. No SD was calculated from an SE, no coefficient was obtained by adding terms, no standardized effect or test statistic was computed, and no values were digitized from figures. The paper does not report across-person diversity or a delayed follow-up. No shared participant sample with another paper is stated, and the pilot is explicitly separate (PDF pp. 3 and 8).
